title: construct-evaluation-surface-for-multilang-pairwise-selection
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: build a repeatable, statistically sound evaluation surface that lets the ML and SRE teams choose between cross-encoder variants (fp16 / int8 quantized / distilled) for multilingual reranking. The surface must expose joint quality × latency curves per locale, tail-latency percentiles, stability under load, and regression flags tied to canned prompt sets and live traffic shadowing.

Background: We currently maintain several cross-encoder families used by the rerank endpoint. Upgrades have repeatedly run into surprises: locale-specific quality regressions, quantized model skew on long contexts, and unexpected tail latency increases when autoscaling interacts with batching. We need a formalized evaluation surface that codifies acceptance criteria and enables automated gating during staged rollouts.

Scope & deliverables:
- Sampling harness that combines stratified offline evaluation (per-locale, per-query-length, per-intent) + shadowed live sampling with configurable traffic weights.
- Per-variant profiles: top-k NDCG, pairwise accuracy, token-level latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), memory footprint, and KV-cache warm-start behavior.
- A regression detector that raises alerts when quality drops exceed configurable thresholds (absolute or relative) on critical locales or segments.
- Dynamic gating rules that map observed latency/quality tradeoffs to traffic allocation (e.g., route x% to compact quantized variant until p99 < 200ms and NDCG drop < 0.5%).
- Canary protocol and automated rollback triggers (quality regression + latency SLO breach).
- Integration with Console dashboards and rollout APIs for visibility and manual overrides.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Evaluation harness can run end-to-end and produce a per-variant report for 10+ locales within 12 hours on staging data.
2) Regression detector implemented and tested against historical upgrade incidents (synth incident tests).
3) Canary flow that transitions from 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% with automated checks at each step and a single-button rollback.
4) Documentation (Confluence) with decision playbook, gating thresholds, and runbook for investigating failures.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Quantized models reduce compute cost but can have subtle quality shifts on low-resource languages. We'll rely on per-locale stratification and heavier offline validation for tail locales.
- Shadowing live traffic increases infra costs and noise; we'll sample adaptively and warmstart KV caches to reduce variance.
- Choosing aggressive gating may slow rollouts; conservative thresholds increase time-to-ship. We'll propose a default conservative policy and allow tighter thresholds for trusted customers/locales.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: Implement sampling harness and per-variant profiling tools (unit tests + staging runs).
- Week 1: Implement regression detector and synthetic incident checks.
- Week 2: Integrate with Console rollout UI and implement canary orchestration.
- Week 3: Run 3 internal upgrade rehearsals, document runbook, and open beta with select customers.

Notes on implementation details:
- Use stratified sampling: locale (top 10 + tail group), query-length buckets (0-32, 33-128, 129+), and intent categories when available.
- Metrics pipeline: emit evaluation metrics to statsd and storage; aggregate in BigQuery and produce per-run artifact JSONs for Console ingestion.
- Latency measurement: measure token-stepped latency plus end-to-end serving latency including queue time. Instrument traces with variant_id, locale, batch_size, and kv_warm flag.
- Regression detector: configurable thresholds and flavoring (absolute delta vs percentile-based). Integrate with PagerDuty and Slack alert channel.

- PR draft (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/4921
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rerank/variant-profiles
